applyTo: "docs/suggestions/**/*.md"
description: "Use when refining human-facing issue markdown in docs/suggestions/** and keep the writing concise, scannable, and documentation-focused rather than planning-focused"

# Issue Doc Rules

- The issue doc itself is the shared issue-level artifact. Do not create a second heavyweight workflow-state document beside it unless the workflow is intentionally changing.
- Keep issue docs human-facing and GitHub-ready so the same file can guide planning chats and later be posted or copied upstream.
- Keep issue prose concise and scannable with short paragraphs, flat bullets, and concrete examples.
- Use inline code for file paths, types, flags, keys, and exported symbols.
- Prefer linking to canonical module docs instead of duplicating long explanations inside issue markdown.
- Do not turn issue docs into changelogs, completion logs, or design-history dumps.
- Do not embed code edits or implementation patches inside the issue doc.
- Keep tense present-focused and plain: describe what the issue covers, not a timeline of what happened.
- Keep tone plain and professional. No emojis.
- When refining an existing issue, preserve useful user-authored phrasing and only restructure the parts needed for clarity, sequencing, or correctness.
